Byomkesh.description: The protagonist, a brilliant and unconventional detective who prefers to call himself a 'Seeker of Truth' rather than a detective.

Ajit.description: Byomkesh's close friend and chronicler, who narrates the stories and often assists in investigations.

Ashutosh Mitra.description: A middle-aged, unmarried man who becomes a target in the gramophone pin mystery.

Prafulla Roy.description: A seemingly amiable insurance agent who is later revealed to be the mastermind behind the gramophone pin murders.

Putiram.description: A servant who brings snacks and tea to Byomkesh and Ajit.

Jayhari Sanyal.description: The first victim of the gramophone pin murders, found dead on Cornwallis Street.

Kailashchandra Moulik.description: A wealthy businessman and the second victim of the gramophone pin murders.

Kali Singh.description: Kailashbabu's chauffeur, detained by the police on suspicion.

Krishnadayal Laha.description: A rich moneylender and another victim of the gramophone pin murders.

Bilash Mullick.description: Ashubabu's lawyer who conspires against him and later absconds with his companion.

Binod.description: Ashubabu's nephew, described as a drunkard and gambler, currently in prison.

Harrison Road.description: A major thoroughfare in Calcutta, known for its bustling traffic and activity.

Whiteway Laidlaw.description: A famous British-era department store in Calcutta, often referenced as a landmark.

New Market.description: A historic and popular shopping area in central Calcutta.

Maidan.description: A large urban park in Calcutta, often used for recreation and public events.

Red Road.description: A prominent road in Calcutta, adjacent to the Maidan.

Calcutta.description: The capital city of West Bengal, India, now known as Kolkata.

Sukiya Street.description: A street in Calcutta, mentioned as the residence of Jayhari Sanyal.

Cornwallis Street.description: A street in Calcutta where the first gramophone pin murder occurs.

Dharmatolla.description: A busy commercial area and road intersection in central Calcutta.

Wellington Street.description: A street in Calcutta, near Dharmatolla, mentioned in the context of a murder.

Jorasanko.description: A neighborhood in Calcutta, known for its cultural and historical significance.

Amherst Street.description: A street in Calcutta, intersecting with Harrison Road.

Nebutola.description: A locality in Calcutta, mentioned as Ashubabu's residence.

Kidderpore.description: A neighborhood in Calcutta, known for its docks and the racecourse.

Bowbazar.description: A central neighborhood in Calcutta, known for its markets and busy streets.

Howrah.description: A city across the river from Calcutta, also referencing the Howrah Bridge.

Howrah Bridge.description: A famous cantilever bridge connecting Calcutta and Howrah.

Jessore.description: A town in present-day Bangladesh, referenced as the supposed location of the real Prafulla Roy.

Burdwan.description: A city in West Bengal, mentioned as the place where Bilash Mullick is expected to be arrested.

Lalbazar.description: The location of Calcutta Police Headquarters.

Sealdah.description: An important railway station and area in Calcutta.

Chowringhee.description: A major road and district in central Calcutta, known for its hotels and landmarks.

Kalighat.description: A locality in Calcutta, famous for its Kali temple.

Circular Road.description: A road in Calcutta, referenced as a tram route.

Jewel Insurance Company.description: The insurance company Prafulla Roy claims to work for.

Daily Kalketu.description: A fictional newspaper reporting on the gramophone pin murders.

Reuters.description: An international news agency, referenced in the discussion about news sources.

Mahabharata.description: An ancient Indian epic, referenced in relation to Arjun's archery skills.

Draupadi.description: A character from the Mahabharata, referenced in the context of her swayamvara.

Arjun.description: A legendary archer from the Mahabharata, referenced for his unparalleled skill.

Deoghar.description: A town in Jharkhand, India, mentioned as the place where Ashubabu met his mistress.

babu.description: A term of respect for a man, especially in Bengal.

dhoti.description: A traditional men's garment, a long piece of cloth wrapped around the waist and legs.

kurta.description: A loose, collarless shirt worn in South Asia.

adda.description: An informal gathering or conversation, usually among friends, often involving intellectual discussion.

paan.description: A preparation combining betel leaf with areca nut and sometimes tobacco, chewed for its stimulant effects.

cheroot.description: A type of cigar with both ends clipped during manufacture, commonly smoked in India.
